response:
Diagnosis from generation 0: all three evaluated signals produced positive Fama-MacBeth slopes but *negative* FF5 alphas. That pattern says the raw spreads are essentially repackaged HML/RMW/CMA exposure — the factor loadings predict more return than the portfolios deliver, so the interaction added no abnormal return beyond the value/profitability factors themselves. The fix is not a better weighting of B/M and ROA; it is to move the interaction onto dimensions FF5 does not span: accounting conservatism (non-cash charges), working-capital accruals, cross-multiple valuation mismatch, balance-sheet *changes*, and time-series (own-history) cheapness. All expressions below also carry at least one quality-exclusive input (dp, cogs, act, lct, lt, re) to satisfy the theme validator.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Non-Cash Charge Valuation Wedge
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that look far cheaper on cash earnings than on reported net income have earnings depressed by heavy non-cash depreciation charges; that gap is conservative accounting quality, not economic weakness, and the market underprices the hidden cash generation.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Both legs are valuation ranks, so the spread is close to HML-neutral by construction and its abnormal return cannot come from a simple cheapness bet — the only surviving content is the depreciation wedge, which FF5 does not price. Industry ranking prevents the signal from becoming a pure capital-intensity sector tilt, and the difference form avoids the doubly-bad-corner problem of rank products.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Working-Capital Accrual Gated Earnings Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1), dp), at)), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: A high earnings yield is a mispricing signal only when the earnings are not manufactured by working-capital build-up; when accruals are negative (cash-conservative), the cheap price reflects neglect, whereas positive-accrual cheap firms are reporting earnings that will reverse.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gate uses balance-sheet accruals constructed directly from act, lct and dp rather than the oancf-vs-ib gap, so the quality channel is the Sloan accrual anomaly — a dimension absent from FF5 and only weakly correlated with RMW. Firms failing the gate score exactly zero (neutral) instead of entering the long leg, which is the value-trap exclusion the story requires and should lift alpha rather than merely re-sorting on cheapness.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Profit-Cheap Versus Asset-Cheap Mismatch
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(at, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that is cheap relative to its gross profit stream but not unusually cheap relative to its asset base is priced below its earning power; a firm that is cheap only on assets is an asset-heavy, low-margin business whose discount is deserved.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This isolates the residual of profit-based cheapness after asset-based cheapness, which is precisely the component of value that HML (a book-to-market factor) leaves unpriced, so a positive FF5 alpha is achievable even though each leg alone is a familiar multiple. Gross profit uses cogs, giving the quality theme a real economic role — cheapness is measured against the most persistent line of the income statement rather than against assets that may be impaired.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Improving Liquidity Cushion Value Gate
EXPRESSION: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 1), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: What separates quality value from value traps is not the static level of balance-sheet strength but its direction: a cheap firm whose working-capital cushion is expanding relative to total liabilities is deleveraging out of the discount, while a cheap firm with an eroding cushion is sliding toward distress.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The generation-0 solvency gate was a static level screen and its spread was absorbed (negatively) by FF5; using the one-year change in the liquidity-to-liabilities ratio tests whether the direction of balance-sheet quality, which no FF5 factor captures, is what carries the abnormal return. It is deliberately a near-controlled contrast with the prior gated-value result, isolating level-versus-change as the design choice.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Own-History Cheapness With Intact Margins
EXPRESSION: MUL(ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5)), INDICATOR(DELTA(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 3), 1), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm trading at the cheap end of its own five-year valuation range is mispriced only if its operating margins have not deteriorated; identical own-history cheapness accompanied by falling gross profitability is a rational repricing of a decaying franchise.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Time-series cheapness is close to orthogonal to the cross-sectional book-to-market that HML spans, which directly addresses the negative-alpha problem of the archive, and the smoothed gross-margin change supplies the quality state that decides whether the de-rating is information or overreaction. Standardizing the time-series rank keeps the passing group signed while margin-deteriorating firms are set to neutral rather than shorted, avoiding a short leg dominated by transient losers.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Dividend Yield Per Unit Of Leverage
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(lt, at)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Cash actually distributed to shareholders is the least manipulable evidence of earnings quality, and a high dividend yield financed from a light liability structure signals genuine undervaluation, whereas the same yield on a heavily levered balance sheet is a payout the firm may not sustain.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Both numerator and denominator are sign-definite (dividends non-negative, liabilities-to-assets positive), so the ratio is monotone across the whole support and avoids the sign discontinuity that sank the earlier volatility-deflated yield. The mechanism — verified cash distribution scaled by balance-sheet obligation — is distinct from the earnings- and book-based multiples that dominate the archive, and dividend yield is only partially spanned by HML and RMW.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE Non-Cash Charge Valuation Wedge---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The construction is internally consistent and the rank-difference does isolate a depreciation-to-price wedge that is plausibly orthogonal to HML, though the reviewer should be aware the surviving content is close to a capital-intensity/dp-to-price tilt that CMA may partially absorb.

---CRITIQUE Working-Capital Accrual Gated Earnings Yield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is structurally the same ZSCORE(WINSOR(yield))×INDICATOR template as the archived Solvency-Gated Enterprise Earnings Yield with only the gate swapped, and the gate itself is a direct restatement of the published Sloan balance-sheet accrual anomaly (with a crude, cash-and-debt-unadjusted accrual definition).

---CRITIQUE Profit-Cheap Versus Asset-Cheap Mismatch---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Differencing GP/P against AT/P mechanically nets out the price scaling and leaves something very close to gross-profits-to-assets, i.e. a rediscovery of Novy-Marx gross profitability that RMW largely spans, contradicting the claim that FF5 leaves it unpriced.

---CRITIQUE Improving Liquidity Cushion Value Gate---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Self-described as a "near-controlled contrast" with the archived gated-value signal, it reuses the identical yield×indicator template with a level-to-change tweak on the gate — a cosmetic variant unlikely to flip an alpha that was negative for portfolio-composition reasons, and its gate overlaps heavily with the accrual gate proposed alongside it.

---CRITIQUE Own-History Cheapness With Intact Margins---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Substituting a time-series (own-history) valuation rank for cross-sectional cheapness is a genuinely different design that plausibly escapes HML spanning, and the margin gate is coherently specified — though the margin-trend leg echoes the archived industry sales-yield signal and the TS_RANK window units should be verified.

---CRITIQUE Dividend Yield Per Unit Of Leverage---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially the long-published dividend-yield anomaly divided by a bounded leverage ratio, it collapses to a large zero mass for non-payers (biasing coverage and portfolio composition), and the stated rationale references a prior signal not in the archive.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Glamour With Working-Capital Bloat
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The sharpest valuation-quality mispricing sits on the overpriced side: firms carrying a rich price relative to the gross profit they actually generate, while simultaneously inflating net working capital, are financing an expensive valuation with soft, reversing accounting numbers and should underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Rather than swapping a gate inside the same yield×indicator template, this flips the economic side of the interaction: the informative corner is expensive-plus-deteriorating-quality, which is where limits to arbitrage bind hardest and where FF5's HML and RMW have the least power because both legs are ranked within industry. Using NEG of the gross-profit yield rather than the inverted multiple keeps negative-gross-profit firms at the expensive extreme instead of flipping their sign, and the product of two non-negative industry ranks makes the top corner unambiguously the doubly-bad firm.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Multiple Agreement Cheapness
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness is credible only when independent accounting bases agree: a firm cheap on book value but expensive on gross profit is an asset-heavy business with no earning power, while a firm cheap on gross profit but expensive on book has already written its assets up; only agreement across both bases identifies genuine underpricing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Price appears in both legs and they are combined with a non-linear MIN rather than a difference, so the scaling does not cancel and the construct cannot collapse to gross-profits-to-assets — the object measured is disagreement across multiples, a dimension RMW does not represent. The quality content enters through which fundamental the market is being asked to capitalize (gross profit versus book assets), so the long leg is cheap-and-earning rather than merely cheap.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cheap And Retiring Net Obligations
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A depressed valuation resolves into returns when the firm is actively shrinking its net obligations: deleveraging transfers enterprise value to equity holders, whereas a cheap firm whose net liabilities keep rising is transferring value to creditors and is a genuine trap.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This abandons the binary yield×indicator template for a continuous product of two non-negative industry ranks, so no firm is parked at an artificial zero and portfolio composition stays stable across time. The quality channel is the change in cash-netted total obligations rather than a static solvency level or a working-capital accrual, which makes it distinct from both the archived solvency gate and the accrual-based proposals, and only loosely related to CMA's asset-growth content.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Obligation-Netted Fundamental To Price
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(che, lt), MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: What equity holders can actually claim is cash, minus all obligations, plus a durable cash-earnings stream; a market capitalization that is small relative to that claim indicates underpricing, whereas a firm whose apparent cheapness disappears once liabilities are netted and earnings are averaged is priced correctly.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Dividends are dropped entirely, which removes the non-payer zero mass and the dependence on a published payout anomaly, and coverage becomes near-universal since cash, liabilities and cash earnings are reported by essentially all firms. The quality element is structural rather than a bolt-on screen: obligations are subtracted from the numerator and the earnings component is a three-year average, so a single peak year or a liability-financed balance sheet cannot generate a high score.
